memory: I confirmed a ~0.006 mm centroid crest causes a local tau_c kink. Lateral shifts (+0.30, +0.60 mm) reduce and relocate the concentration, leaving a persistent elongated residual (~0.0025 N·m at +0.60 mm). A 0.5 mm neoprene spacer at +0.60 mm reduced that residual to ~0.0009 ±0.0002 N·m, broadened the contact band, lowered peak pressure, and smeared micro-slip onset. Conclusion: geometry dominates the large jump; pad compliance attenuates but does not eliminate the offset-dependent residual. Current position: quantify how residual scales with compliance/thickness.
openQuestion: How does residual tau_c amplitude change with spacer thickness (0.25 mm and 0.75 mm) at +0.60 mm offset?
